title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In chapter III of the 1986 notes ('Réseaux via découpages'), Grothendieck builds a combinatorial, poset-flavoured 'tame topology' on a découpage (dissection) L. Page 18 defines the ingredients:
- A 'partie fermée modérée' (closed tame part) is a finite disjoint union of closed pseudo-découpages T_i that are pairwise in 'position relative modérée'. This means every pair {a,b}, with a in the boundary §T_i and b in the boundary §T_j, belongs to Dép_2(L).
- The T_i are uniquely determined: they are the connected components.
- The boundary (hat, or a superscript circle on this page) of such a part is the union of the boundaries of its components. It is empty exactly when the part is ∅ or all of L.

This page states closure properties of the class of closed tame parts.

(1) Let X and Y be closed tame parts in relative tame position. Then:
- X∩Y is again a closed tame part, and its boundary satisfies (X∩Y)° ⊂ X°∪Y°.
- X and Y have a least upper bound in the poset (under inclusion) of closed tame parts. This is denoted X ∪_mod Y and is the 'tame union'.
- Its boundary satisfies (X ∪_mod Y)° ⊂ X°∪Y°.

(2) The same holds for a finite family (X_i) that is pairwise in relative tame position: the intersection ⋂X_i is tame, the X_i have a tame sup, and (∪_mod X_i)° ⊂ ⋃ X_i°. The left-margin proof sketch reduces the finite case to the case of two parts, presumably by induction.

(3) Example: [a,b] ∪_mod [b,c] = [a,c], whereas in general the set-theoretic union [a,b]∪[b,c] ≠ [a,c]. For instance, if a is the least and c the greatest element, equality holds exactly when b is comparable to every element.

The right margin introduces a notation: for an arbitrary subset A, the smallest closed tame part containing A. The example given is A = {0,1/2,1} ↦ [0,1]. So 'closed tame' here behaves like an order-convex / interval-type hull, not like topological closure.

Page 20 then draws the conclusion: L is totally ordered iff for every b, L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L_{≤b} ∪ L_{≥b} (= L). It then passes to locally closed tame parts and a tame difference X \_mod Y.

Purpose: to obtain a lattice-like ('réseau') calculus of tame parts. Union is replaced by a hull-type join, which is needed to define tame complements and differences and ultimately to recover lattices or ordered structures from découpages.
errors: The transcription has the hypothesis as 'pos. gén. modérée'. The image reads 'en pos. rel. modérée', matching the definition at the bottom of page 18.

The boundary inclusions and the existence of the sup are stated without proof; only a marginal reduction to two parts is sketched. They are plausible under the page-18 definitions, but whether X∩Y is again a finite disjoint union of closed pseudo-découpages in relative tame position depends on unstated properties of Dép_2.
The parenthetical about when [a,b]∪[b,c] = [a,c] is garbled. The intended statement (made explicit on page 20) is: with a = min and c = max, equality holds iff b is comparable to every element.

ideas.what: Class of closed tame parts of a découpage closed under finite intersection, with boundary of intersection contained in union of boundaries
ideas.modern_name: Boolean/lattice structure of definable (tame) closed sets; boundary calculus as in o-minimal or semialgebraic geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s–1998); the program of tame topology is Grothendieck's own (Esquisse 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces 'topologie modérée' only programmatically; this combinatorial découpage version is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Tame union X ∪_mod Y defined as least upper bound in the poset of closed tame parts (a hull or closure-operator join), differing from the set union
ideas.modern_name: Join in the lattice of closed sets of a closure operator (abstract convexity / convex geometries; order-convex hull)

ideas.what: Characterisation of total order by L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L_{≤b} ∪ L_{≥b} for all b (completed on next page)

missed.claim: This page is part of an unpublished, fully combinatorial axiomatisation of 'tame topology' via découpages and the lattice of closed tame parts. It is a concrete instance of the Esquisse programme that the literature (which went the o-minimal way) did not follow. On its own the page is routine closure-operator bookkeeping.
missed.quote: X et Y ont une borne sup. dans l'ens. des parties fermées modérées. On note cette partie X ∪_mod Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of documentary interest: it shows Grothendieck's tame topology developed as an order- and lattice-theoretic calculus rather than a model-theoretic one.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine lattice and closure statements in a nonstandard setting. Their main interest is as evidence of the unpublished combinatorial 'topologie modérée' project, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'en pos. rel. modérée', not 'en pos. gén. modérée'.
'fermée' is inserted above the line, so the conclusion reads 'X∩Y est une partie fermée modérée'. The boxed formula (X∩Y)° ⊂ X°∪Y° stands in the upper right.
The family hypothesis likely reads 'mutuellement en pos. rel. modérée' (consistent with page 18).
Right margin: reads roughly 'Notation: pour une partie A ... la plus petite partie fermée modérée qui contient A ... ex. A = {0,1/2,1}, [0,1]'.
Last lines: '(quand a plus petit élément, c plus grand élément, on a =, b étant comparable à tout autre élément de L)' — the next page confirms this reading.
